In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Pol IV/Rdr2-dependent transcripts are the precursors to siRNAs and that these transcripts are distinct from Pol II-dependent mRNAs.
Pol IV/RD2-dependent transcripts are the precursors for siRNA biogensis.
Pol IV/Rdr2 dependent transcripts are not primary transcripts, but rather are the result of Pol IV/Rdr 2 dependent transcription of Pol II dependent primary transcripts.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Pol IV/Rdr2-dependent transcripts are 5′ capped, 3′ uncapped, and lack introns.
Pol IV/RD2-dependent transcripts are 24-nt siRNA precursors that are transcribed from both DNA strands of the RdDM loci and are distinct from Pol II-dependent transcription.
Pol IV/RD2-dependent transcripts are the precursors of siRNAs that are essential for RdDM, which is a key epigenetic mechanism to maintain the stability of the genome in plants.
The main takeaway from our work is that

Pol IV-dependent transcription is widespread in the Arabidopsis genome, but the transcriptional machinery that Pol IV utilizes is distinct from that of RNA Pol II, and that the transcription of Pol IV-dependent loci is subject to regulation.
Pol IV-dependent transcription occurs at a large number of loci, and these transcripts are processed into siRNAs that direct RdDM.
Pol IV/RD2-dependent transcripts have been identified for the first time at a genome-wide scale.
